target.title: fix(vydra): apply request policy to media generation requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users routing Vydra media generation through configured request headers, a proxy dispatcher, or private-network policy could have polling or generated-media downloads leave that configured transport path after submission succeeded.

## Why This Change Was Made

Vydra now prepares one request policy and carries it through each applicable stage: image and video submit, poll, and download, plus speech submit and download. Same-origin generated assets retain the provider authorization and configured headers; cross-origin assets receive neither. Generated-media error and success bodies remain bounded by one wall-clock deadline, with stable Vydra timeout errors when the guarded request abort wins the body-read deadline race.

This is an AI-assisted contribution prepared for Alix-007.

## User Impact

Operators can rely on configured Vydra headers, proxy dispatch, and private-network opt-in throughout a media-generation operation. Provider credentials and custom headers no longer leak to cross-origin generated-asset URLs.

## Evidence

### Exact revision and CI

- Exact PR head: `c91a9cc649653484a77923dc224f6d376e0ddc8c`.
- Frozen branch base: `047232bd16e407cf53762eb6ffa80d400b1d249e`.
- Full diff SHA-256: `0e9b1b0a5e753ecec738acef4d729a78f98179441fea6d65fb51f96baadc7ae4` (8 files, +270/-62).
- [Exact-head upstream CI run 29671601040](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29671601040): completed successfully; no failed jobs. `checks-node-changed`, `check-test-types`, and `check-lint` all passed.
- Current `main` has no changes to the touched Vydra or governing video/TTS request-contract paths since the frozen base; the merge tree is conflict-free and GitHub reports the PR mergeable.

### Public TLS submit -> poll -> download proof

[Secretless fork run 29671816520](https://github.com/Alix-007/openclaw/actions/runs/29671816520) detached to the exact PR head and exercised the production Vydra video provider through two independent public HTTPS origins. The run used the official `cloudflared` 2026.7.2 Linux AMD64 asset pinned to SHA-256 `ec905ea7b7e327ff8abdde8cb64697a2152de74dbcdbf6aec9db8364eb3886cd`.

The driver asserted the exact six-request sequence for two complete flows. Same-origin submit, poll, and download carried authorization and the configured policy header. The second flow used a distinct generated-asset origin; submit and poll retained provider headers while download carried neither authorization nor the custom header.

```text
PROOF_REF exact_head=c91a9cc649653484a77923dc224f6d376e0ddc8c
EXTERNAL_TLS endpoint_class=two-independent-trycloudflare-origins protocol=https
SAME_ORIGIN stages=submit,poll,download authorization=present policy_header=present
CROSS_ORIGIN stages=submit,poll,download provider_headers=present,present,absent
PROOF_RESULT flows=2 status=passed full_hostnames=redacted authorization_values=redacted
PROOF_CLEANUP tunnels=stopped origins=closed
```

The exact-head focused lane in the same run passed:

```text
Test Files  4 passed (4)
Tests       26 passed (26)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 23.19s
```

It covers:

- image same-origin header retention and cross-origin authorization/custom-header omission;
- direct video submit -> poll -> download policy propagation;
- speech same-origin authenticated download;
- successful and non-2xx dripping bodies under one deadline;
- normalized/redacted provider errors, null bodies, body-stream failures, overflow, and early 200 body failures without timeout over-classification.

### Request-policy contract boundary

Caller-specific `ssrfPolicy` is part of the image-generation request contract and is propagated by the Vydra image path. It is not a field on either the current [`VideoGenerationRequest`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2f00a417edde2112dd0c4c8f230e9395b496f378/src/video-generation/types.ts#L62-L83) or [`SpeechSynthesisRequest`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/2f00a417edde2112dd0c4c8f230e9395b496f378/src/tts/provider-types.ts#L54-L61), and their runtime entry points do not supply one. Video carries its configured model-provider `allowPrivateNetwork`, dispatcher, and headers; speech retains its resolved authorization headers only for same-origin downloads. This matches the existing capability contracts and sibling provider behavior without adding a new SDK request surface in this PR.

Fresh independent Codex reviews checked the frozen policy delta, the body-deadline race repair, and the proof workflow. No accepted actionable findings remain.

### Remaining proof boundary

No live Vydra account or real generated Vydra artifact was used. The external proof uses controlled Vydra-compatible public DNS/TLS endpoints and a non-secret proof token, so it proves production request routing, origin separation, header behavior, deadlines, and cleanup without claiming live-provider availability or schema behavior.
